{{Quote|Growing up in the capital city of Pelek Baw, there were ''scores'' of kids. Of course, there were also scores of ''parents''.|Azita Cruuz|<ref name="Mace Windu 3" />}}
'''Pelek Baw''' was the [[capital]] [[city]] of<ref name="Mace Windu 3" /> the [[planet]]<ref name="Force Users">{{EncyclopediaCite|Mace Windu and Other Users of the Force}}</ref> [[Haruun Kal]]. [[Azita Cruuz]], a [[human]] [[Homeworld|native]] of the world, grew up alone in the city as an orphan and encountered many other [[Youngling|children]] there who still had [[parent]]s. At one point, she passed through a [[tree]]-lined square of tan buildings that was full of these families as she sadly clutched a [[book]] to her chest. As an adult, Cruuz told [[Jedi Knight]] [[Mace Windu]], also a native of Haruun Kaal, about Pelek Baw when he asked if his memory of Haruun Kaal having lots of children was correct while the pair [[Mission to Ro Mira|traveled]] together<ref name="Mace Windu 3" /> by [[48 BBY]].<ref name="Date">[[Mace Windu 3|''Mace Windu'' 3]] establishes its events take place prior to [[Mace Windu]]'s entry into the [[Jedi High Council]]. ''[[Master & Apprentice]]'' establishes that Windu is part of the Jedi Council at the [[time]] of [[Nim Pianna]]'s [[Mutiny on the Advent|death]], which ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates to [[48 BBY]]. Therefore, the events of ''Mace Windu'' 3 must take place by that [[Standard year|year]].</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
In the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], Pelek Baw appeared in a flashback in the [[Mace Windu 3|third issue]] of the [[2024]] [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] miniseries ''[[Star Wars: Mace Windu]]''. The issue was written by [[Marc Bernardin]], illustrated by [[Georges Jeanty]], and published by [[Marvel Comics]]<ref name="Mace Windu 3" /> on [[April 17]], 2024.<ref name="Marvel">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/110344/star_wars_mace_windu_2024_3|text=Star Wars: Mace Windu (2024) #3}}</ref> The [[Pelek Baw/Legends|city]] originated in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, where it first appeared in [[Matthew Stover]]'s [[2003]] novel, [[Shatterpoint (novel)|''Shatterpoint'']].<ref name="Shatterpoint">[[Shatterpoint (novel)|''Shatterpoint'']]</ref>
